sense: all over a place, all through a time

terms.gloss: throughout, all over; all through (a time)
evidence: Catull. 101.1: multās per gentēs et multa per aequora vectus
Cato Agr. 37: per hiemem lūcubrātiōne haec facitō
terms.comment: All over a space or all through a time: per tōtam domum, all over the house; per hiemem, all through the winter; per tōtam noctem, all night long.

terms.grammar: ablative with tōtus, without a preposition
evidence: Ov. Met. 11.609: nūlla domō tōtā est
terms.comment: A place qualified by tōtus usually stands in the ablative alone (see in).

evidence: Ov. F. 3.525: passim disjecta per herbās

phrases.latin: multās per gentēs et multa per aequora vectus adveniō
phrases.english: carried through many peoples and over many seas, I come
do these jobs through the winter by lamplight

phrases.latin: plēbs venit ac viridēs passim disjecta per herbās pōtat
phrases.english: the people come and drink, scattered here and there all over the green grass

phrases.latin: nox erat et terrās animālia fessa per omnēs ālituum pecudumque genus sopor altus habēbat
phrases.english: it was night, and throughout all lands deep sleep held the tired creatures, the birds and the beasts

phrases.latin: tempora cum causīs Latium dīgesta per annum lāpsaque sub terrās ortaque signa canam
phrases.english: I shall sing of the seasons set out through the Latin year, and their causes, and the stars that set below the earth and rise

sources: Lewis & Short: per · Lewis & Short: totus · Lewis & Short: passim
